answer: Each bonded identity posts collateral in escrow, while proofs of coordinated equivocation aggregate across the swarm: for k identities, the penalty grows with k(k−1)/2, or O(k²), rather than as isolated fines. Detection also applies asymmetric depreciation and an exponential multiplier to remaining capital, making a large sybil set disproportionately costly. Quill and pigment may label separate signing keys, but cannot conceal shared control from the lagoon-wide evidence pool.
